purpose: A nine-figure source-image trial in which six stronger anatomy/pathway plates replace redundant course-made figures and three unique images add non-duplicated detail. Corrected web instruction and interactions remain intact.

visuals.title: A labelled neuron as an anatomical reference
visuals.releaseBlocker: Clear the embedded image's reuse provenance or replace it with an approved redraw before promotion or export.
visuals.altText: Stylized multipolar neuron labelled with dendrites, cell body, nucleus, mitochondrion, axon, myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier, Schwann cells, synapse, and axon terminals.
visuals.longDescription: Branching dendrites surround a cell body containing a nucleus and mitochondrion. A long axon extends through repeated myelin segments separated by nodes of Ranvier and ends in branching axon terminals. The plate identifies Schwann cells because it depicts peripheral myelin; oligodendrocytes provide myelin in the central nervous system. This is one useful neuron form, not a universal neuron shape.

visuals.title: Neural tissue under magnification
visuals.altText: False-colour micrograph showing interconnected neural cells.
visuals.longDescription: Blue branching processes form a dense network. Several yellow cell bodies and one larger purple supporting cell are visible. The still image shows cellular organization but cannot show signal direction or conduction speed.

visuals.title: How roots connect a spinal nerve to the cord
visuals.releaseBlocker: Clear the embedded image's reuse provenance or replace it with an approved redraw before promotion or export.
visuals.altText: Spinal-cord cross-section labelling central gray matter, surrounding white matter, dorsal and ventral horns, dorsal and ventral roots, dorsal-root ganglion, spinal nerve, and sensory and motor paths.
visuals.longDescription: Butterfly-shaped gray matter lies centrally and white matter surrounds it. Sensory neuron fibres enter through the dorsal root, with the sensory neuron cell body in the dorsal-root ganglion. Motor neuron fibres leave through the ventral root. The roots join as a mixed spinal nerve containing both sensory and motor axons.

visuals.title: Functional regions of the cerebral cortex
visuals.altText: Side view of a brain with cortical lobes and selected motor, sensory, language, auditory, taste, and visual regions labelled.
visuals.longDescription: The frontal lobe includes prefrontal, premotor, primary motor, and motor-speech regions. The parietal lobe includes primary and association somatosensory regions. The temporal lobe includes primary and association auditory regions and a sensory-speech region. The occipital lobe includes primary and association visual regions. These boundaries are a simplified map; complex functions depend on distributed networks.

visuals.title: Anatomy behind the five-part reflex pathway
visuals.releaseBlocker: Clear the embedded image's reuse provenance or replace it with an approved redraw before promotion or export.
visuals.altText: Five-part reflex pathway showing a skin receptor, sensory neuron, spinal integration centre with an interneuron, motor neuron, and muscle effector.
visuals.longDescription: A receptor in the skin connects by a sensory neuron to the spinal cord. Within the spinal gray matter, an interneuron represents central integration. A motor neuron leaves the cord and reaches a muscle effector. The image simplifies a reflex pathway and does not show every interneuron, inhibitory branch, or ascending pathway to the brain.

visuals.title: Detailed eye anatomy
visuals.releaseBlocker: Clear the embedded image's reuse provenance or replace it with an approved redraw before promotion or export.
visuals.altText: Detailed cross-section of the human eye with major structures labelled.
visuals.longDescription: The diagram labels the cornea, aqueous humour, iris, pupil, lens, suspensory ligament, ciliary body, vitreous humour, sclera, choroid, retina, fovea centralis, optic disc, blood vessels, and optic nerve. Light enters through the cornea and pupil, is focused by the lens, crosses the vitreous humour, and reaches the retina.

visuals.title: Outer, middle, and inner ear anatomy
visuals.altText: Cross-section of the human ear with outer, middle, and inner structures labelled.
visuals.longDescription: The pinna leads to the auditory canal and tympanum. The ossicles connect the tympanum to the oval window. The cochlea and semicircular canals form the inner ear, the auditory nerve exits toward the brain, and the Eustachian tube connects the middle ear with the throat region.

visuals.title: Endocrine cells and capillaries
visuals.altText: Endocrine cells arranged around a dense capillary network.
visuals.longDescription: Hormone-producing cells surround branching capillaries. Arrows show blood entering the network and leaving after secreted hormone has entered extracellular fluid and then the bloodstream. Only cells with compatible receptors respond to the circulating hormone.

visuals.title: Hypothalamus and pituitary pathways
visuals.altText: Hypothalamus and pituitary diagram comparing posterior neural release with anterior portal control.
visuals.longDescription: On the posterior side, hypothalamic neurosecretory cells make ADH and oxytocin, move them down axons, and release them from posterior-pituitary terminals. On the anterior side, hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones enter portal blood and regulate anterior-pituitary hormone secretion. Target boxes connect each pituitary hormone with responsive tissues or glands.
